# OLYMPUS v0.0.20, "Stack and clear: never pinned, never masked, heard, and told why": the build sheet

> This is the round's build sheet as written before the build (2026-11-16), kept whole as the contract the roles built to, with §15 added after the build: the round's resolutions. §15 wins over any line above it that it contradicts. DESIGN.md's log of 2026-11-16 carries the decisions. Where the sheet says v0.0.19's lines or a `// (v0.0.20 …)` anchor, the lead stripped those anchors before the release.


Written 2026-11-16 for the round's four implementers (A, B, C, D) and the lead, who integrates. It is the contract between roles that build in parallel without talking. It sits on v0.0.19 as `.run/v019-design/full/sheet.md` gives it, which sits on v0.0.18 as `.run/v018-design/sheet.md` gives it. Where a release as built differs from its sheet, the code decides and the role says so in its handoff.

Where this sheet is silent, the docs decide: DESIGN.md and the user's rules first, then TECH §1.3, then the sections it cites, then the four lens notes it merges (`.run/v020-design/user.md`, `feel.md`, `drill.md`, `card.md`; each item below names its source, and "as designed" means the mechanism, constants and tests there stand unless this sheet changes them). My own choices are marked (my call). Every conflict between the four notes, and between them and v0.0.18 and v0.0.19, is settled in §0.

**Lines.** The lens notes quote v0.0.17's lines (`3c3a512`). Main's working tree already carries v0.0.18's merges in progress (bundle.js's `giveWayOut` is at :2119 there, `gapHold` :2148, `entryGo` :2046; shoothouse.js's `twoTick` :868, `twoFire` :990, `endLeg` :1399), and v0.0.19 moves the #2's code to `house-two.js`. So **every hunk is named by its function**, and a line is only a pointer.

**The release.** The shoot house stays the pilot (the user, 2026-11-11: "This mission should be perfected before you spend any token on any other mission"). v0.0.18 made the options follow the gun and brought the kit; v0.0.19 brings the rest of the kit, the team and the first live men. v0.0.20 is the round of what a player meets in every lane and that still reads as a prototype:

1. **The bodies and the line (A)**: nobody is ever pinned by a body; your #2 never fires through you, and you keep out of his sector; he enters on your heels; he gets round you or tells you why he cannot; the pair keeps together in the hall.
2. **The room (B)**: AT THE DOOR's five as the user's P3-j drew it, on every lane; Fix on the cold line does what the tower says; leaving a room as doctrine has it (his status, "Coming out!", the last man marks the jamb, drawn); the far leg covered ("Moving!", "Move!"); his call-outs shorten your take-in; a door moves as it was opened; your corner's aid held as long as you want it.
3. **The card (C)**: the debrief gives the cause of every missed par, the instructor's dummy apart; pars a sheet can meet; six aspects to score; who speaks seen over his head; the plaques and the timer off the room; GO or NO-GO and the next sheet up; the session's sheets side by side; the run exported and replayed in node; the plan view.
4. **The sound and the look (D)**: the shot bangs where the ear listens; the house speaks, every line heard; a shot lights the room; the door's knock at its stop; the waiting samples scored in play from the Esc menu; one helmet in one place; the loadout screen shows the marine.

**Merge order**: stage 0 (the lead), then A, B, D, C. C reads every other role's records, so it merges last; D's `spokenMs` is written at stage 0, so C never waits on D.

**Ship rules** (my call):
- Items 1 to 25 of §1 ship in v0.0.20.
- **The voice (item 7)** ships its code; it is the default only if `house-voiced` (at least 95% heard) and `voice-render` pass at D's merge. Otherwise V-a (today's) stays the default, V-c is on `&voice=c` and the To score page, and the Standby fix ships alone.
- **The plan view (item 26)** ships if `house-trace`, `house-debrief` and `ui-houseplan` are green on the last merge. Otherwise none of `houseplan.js` reaches main and it leads v0.0.21; the trace (`R.house.$trace`, runtime only) may ship without it.

**If v0.0.19 shipped without L** (its ship rule allows it, its §0 and §9 item 10): L's four roles finish first, and their merge is stage 0's step 0. The roles of this sheet start from the stage-0 tree either way. If L is still red when they start, every hunk marked **(L)** below is left out of the role's patch and listed in its handoff, and it lands with L. Its gauges keep F38 to F44.

**What the user must feel.**
- Walk a step aside at GO and press T on "Clear the room" with your #2 in your way: he steps off your line within 0.6 s and you are in the room, never frozen. Backspace always gives you your feet.
- Stand on your #2's line to his man: he holds his pair, says "Line!", and fires 0.15 s after you step off. Drift into his sector before "Clear!": the DI says "You're in his sector. Back to your point."
- On the private by the keys, he is in the room 1.6 s behind you, not 2.9 s, and takes his own man.
- Leaving room 1: "Room clear!", his "Up.", your "Coming out!", his "Last man." as he passes the door, and a chalk X on the jamb, drawn from his hand's stroke.
- In room 3, "Moving!", "Move!", and his eyes on the far leg as you walk it; "Hostage, far leg!" before you see the card.
- The instructor's brief, LOAD, MAKE READY, "Lane A. Standby.", GO, your #2's calls and your own are heard, in voices made by code. The tower never cuts the brief.
- Your shot is a bang, not a click with a tail. In a dark room, it lights the floor for its flash.
- The tier one's clean lane says "Clean." and GO, not "He fired first. Set a Watch on your corner". The recruit's card names what cost him the par, and a par he can meet.
- From the Esc menu, "To score" changes the helmet on your #2, the stack's marks, the walk, the shot and the voice live, and "Copy my picks" gives the text to paste back.

**The user's rules hold over every section:** we only know what we know (a call names only what its speaker identified; the plan view shows the truth only after the lane); never a dead end; nothing pops in or out of view; AZERTY labels on physical codes; every image and sound by code; one loadout for every sheet; no overlapping UI; the look chosen from numbered samples the user scores (nothing of the look changes by default until picked); the standard lane is v0.0.19's to the byte unless this sheet names the change (§0 item 30 lists every mover).

**Kept as built and starred:** "Bang" (scored 100, 100, 100 on 2026-11-15) and its four B goldens, its sound included (§0 item 21); "Pairs" (100, 2026-11-08); hit card B (★ 99); P3-j's band (★ 100); the R-7 as G2; the tower's macros and their words; the row ids every bot, the instinct and the gauges key on; HOUSE1's and WHEEL_S4's goldens and X4's plans; F1 to F44, never loosened.

**Rules of the round:**
- Edit only your own files and named hunks (§2). Report any other edit needed, exactly, in your handoff.
- No commits, tags, pushes, releases or promotions. Never touch `.play/`, :8200, :8201, `../longhaul` or `../tradecraft`.
- Scratch goes under `/private/tmp/claude-501/olympus-build/v020/<role>/`. Your handoff goes in `.run/v020/<role>.md` (it survives a reboot): CHANGELOG bullets, doc text, the figures before and after, the pin's moved cells with the item that moved each (§3 step 5), every edit outside your list, the stubs you tested against.
- Worktrees: `git worktree add --detach .claude/worktrees/v020-<role> v0.0.19`, then `git -C <wt> apply .run/v020/stage0.patch`.
- Four roles share the machine: the runner with `JOBS=2` (my call), and only `QUICK=1` or a file with its separator (`'house-unpinned ›'`). Heavy suites wait for the lead's quiet-machine run (§9). While `lsof -nP -iTCP:8200 -sTCP:LISTEN` answers and the Mac has had input in the last 5 minutes, `JOBS=1`.
- A quick file stays under 3 s of CPU, and any whole lane is heavy unless it is one sheet on one seed (v0.0.19 §0 item 26).

**Ports:** A 8230, B 8231, C 8232, D 8233, reviews 8234 and 8235, lead 8236 (`OLYMPUS_TEST_PORT` for single browser suites; the runner claims 8240 to 8249 itself). Kill every server you start.

**Interfaces first.** Each role writes §4's exports as stubs with the shapes given, then fills them, and tests against its own stub of another role's export until that role merges.

**Integration.** As v0.0.19's: the stage-0 tree is the base, `B=$(cat .run/v020/base.tree)`; each role's patch is

```
git -C <wt> add -N . && git -C <wt> diff $B > .run/v020/<role>.patch
```

The lead applies them with `git apply --3way` in the merge order, running `QUICK=1 node tests/run.mjs` after each. Before its final run, each role rebases onto the integrated tree the roles before it left (`git -C <wt> checkout -- . && git -C <wt> apply <integrated.patch>`, then its own on top with `--3way`).

31. **`ENTRY_WAIT_MS` and `HEELS_WAIT_MS`** (drill D2) are one number: `ENTRY_WAIT_MS` becomes 400 ms, and no second name is made.
32. **The tower's wait on the PA is sim.** FL-3 places it "in `shoothouse.js`'s tower sequence". The house's readiness is `shoothouse.js houseReady` (handling.js `lineReady` calls it first, for the current command: its `ready` says when the next one may be posted) and its commands go through `houseOnCmd`. Settled (cross-check):
    - **The text.** `houseOnCmd(state, bus, def)` is not given the PA's words: `handling.js onRangeCmd` (read-only) says them with `hashPick(def.say, 'range-cmd', seed, i)` and passes `i` as a fourth argument. D's `houseOnCmd` line takes that `i` and reads `R.cmd.text ?? hashPick(def.say, 'range-cmd', state.meta.seed, i)`, the same call, and `house-pace` asserts it equals the 'say' fact's text.
    - **The instructor speaks twice at the brief.** At 0.05 s the PA says the brief (35 words, 10.75 s spoken) and, the same tick, `houseOnCmd`'s 'brief' case has `chiefSays` say `HOUSE_CHIEF.brief` with the gravity (27 words, 8.35 s), both by the instructor (p146 on 48213; `says-full.mjs`). His lines queue (item 7), so the brief ends at 19.15 s, not 10.8 s, and a LOAD posted at 10.8 s would be queued behind the speech past its own hold (6.14 s) and dropped. So `R.paUntilMs` chains every line of the instructor's outside the lane: `R.paUntilMs = Math.max(R.paUntilMs ?? 0, now) + spokenMs(text)`, written by `houseOnCmd` for the PA's line and by `chiefSays` (D's one line) for his speech. LOAD then comes at about 19.2 s (3.1 s today).
    - **Which commands wait.** `houseReady` returns false while `now < R.paUntilMs` for the current commands `brief`, `load`, `ready`, `stop`, `clear` and `wash`, before its switch. Never for `standby` (GO is posted by `armGo` at its drawn time through `R.next`) or `go` (Stop comes when the lane is done), so nothing waits during the lane, and the chain is not written between GO's arming and Stop.
    - **It ships with item 7's code whatever the voice's ship rule decides**: it is sim, and the pin must not depend on an audio setting.
    Pairs, Bang and the stress course never read it.

Bests and GOs in `localStorage['olympus.house']` (`{ v: 1, runs: [...] }`, the last `HOUSE_RUNS_MAX` 200, try and catch, never in the save); the picker shows each sheet's best and its GOs; after a GO "Again as" leads with the next sheet up; after a NO-GO, "Again from room n" (the weak room's setup). Nothing is locked.
21. **The grid** (C; card.md C6 less the ghost). `houseGrid(sheets)`, "Bang"'s `gridTable` form: a row a leg, a column a sheet played on this seed this session, each cell the leg's time against its par in `legWords`' words.
22. **One helmet** (D; §0 items 2 and 12). `HELMET_DRAWN_AS = { regular, elite, opa }` (helmets.js) and `STACK_DRAWN_AS` (the stack's marks), both empty until the user picks; the world figure, the doll (`worn.js`) and the hit card's man read `look.helm` and `look.mark`, the trim from the faction (Mars `#C8322A`, UN `#3A7AD8`, OPA none). Built after v0.0.19 L-look's mask hunk in helmets.js **(L)**. Unset, every pixel is v0.0.19's.
23. **The loadout's marine** (D; user.md U-7). The gear doll beside the four faces, from the loadout being chosen, applied to a scratch copy of the fill's kit (`loadout.js applyLoadout`), redrawn on each change; a device pouch drawn by `DEVICES[model].look`; `gear.js gearOfLoadout(code)`; the paint under v0.0.18's 4 ms × k.
24. **The corner aid** (B and D; user.md U-9, §0 items 33 and 34). B: `corner.js aidHoldMs(rung, setting)`, 'always' `AID_HOLD_MS[0]` (to domination), 'off' 0; `cornerAidLook` reads `state.$aid`; `CORNER_POINT` built, 'authored'. D: the row "Corner aid: by rung / always / off" (`olympus.cornerAid`).
25. **The run's export** (C; card.md C7). The page keeps the save at GO and each non-empty input (`{ n, input }`, stop motion's presses included), at most `RUN_INPUTS_MAX` 24,000. `n` is the count of the loop's calls into the sim since GO (each `step(1, input)`, whether or not the clock moved), never `state.clock.tick` or `ms`: in stop motion the clock stands while presses are made, and a log keyed on the clock loses them (CLAUDE.md, the runner and the bots: "key it on the ms and the act together"). `tests/replay-run.mjs` steps once per `n`, with the logged input where there is one and none between; the end card's "Export the run" gives `{ game, version, scene, seed, sheet, par, loadout, atGo, inputs, sheetHash }`; `tests/replay-run.mjs` loads `atGo`, steps the inputs and prints the run sheet. No "drawn" word this round.
26. **The plan view** (C; card.md C2; last, under the ship rule). `traceTick` from `houseRules` every `TRACE_MS` 100 into `R.house.$trace` (runtime only; at most `TRACE_MAX` 6,000), both men and each lane door's leaf, and **(L)** the live men; `house-debrief.js debriefOf(state)` (pure; nothing else in src/sim reads `$trace`, a source scan); `houseplan.js` (Canvas2D, north up, `PLAN_PX_M` 16, or 20 at 1,600 px wide or more), the scrubber at `REPLAY_RATES` [1, 2, 4], a fault clicked seeks to `atMs − SEEK_LEAD_MS` 1,500, a stand clicked opens its truth card at the left as "Bang" has it; the hot wash's take-in bars move into the scrubber's lanes; no scroll at 1024 × 768 or 1600 × 900.

## 3. Stage 0 (the lead, on v0.0.19's tag, before the roles start)

Each step but 2 and 4 is byte-identical: `QUICK=1 node tests/run.mjs`, `house-pin`, `'house-flawless-quick ›'` and `'house-flawless-keys ›'` give v0.0.19's figures.

0. **If L is not in v0.0.19**: L's four patches merged as v0.0.19 §9 checks them, if they are green; else nothing, and every **(L)** hunk waits (the opening rule).
1. **The seams.**
   - `src/core/speech.js`, whole and pure: `SPOKEN_WORD_MS` 300, `SPOKEN_LEAD_MS` 250, `spokenMs(text) → ms` (words split on spaces; numbers as said by voices.js's rule later, one word a token until then). Its header says it is the one helper the sim's tower wait, the voice and the marks read.
   - `carry.js lineMasked(from, to, bodies, opts) → null` (the stub), and `MASK_R_M` 0.3.
   - `state.$aid` and `state.$look` named where the runtime keys are listed (stripped as every `$` key is).
2. **The #2's P-12** (§0 item 15): `TWO_P12_DEFAULT` true. `two-p12`, F34 and `'house-flawless-team ›'` must be green with it; the pin is re-recorded and every moved cell printed in `.run/v020/lead.md`. If the user has answered v0.0.19's question "No", this step is skipped.
3. **The anchors**, one comment line per role, separated by at least one unchanged line, each reading `// (v0.0.20 <role>)`:
   - cqb.js's rule list: A's warn anchor after `cqb-corner` (the last warn rule, cqb.js:566), A's note anchor and B's note anchor before `cqb-door`. The instinct ranks by tone first and by list order within a tone (instinct.js's header, "weighed ... within each tone"), so a warn rule leads every note, `cqb-walk` included, wherever it sits; within the warns, `cqb-funnel` (:551) still leads `cqb-two-out` in a doorway, which is meant;
   - enter-and-clear.js's beats: A's, then B's;
   - bundle.js's kinds, after v0.0.19's: A, then B (no C anchor: C has no bundle.js hunk);
   - `tests/house-fumble.test.mjs` `KNOWN`: one unchanged comment line between the `pin` entry and the `cold-fix` entry, which are adjacent today (v018-net's file, lines 122 to 127): A deletes one and B the other, and two deletions with no unchanged line between them conflict in `git apply --3way`;
   - team.js `TEAM_WORDS`: A, then B;
   - courses.js `HOUSE_CHIEF`: A, then C; `HOUSE_CHIEF.one`: C;
   - shoothouse.js `FAULT_WORDS` and `FAULT_PAPER`: A;
   - ui/cards/house.js `FAULT_MARKS`: A.
   The lead deletes them before the release.
4. **The saves.** Two v0.0.19 saves in `tests/saves/`, gzipped, made by v0.0.19's code, with their `game-upgrade` cases:
   - the private on the standard loadout between LOAD and MAKE READY (the cold Fix and the PA's wait load over it);
   - the corporal mid-room 3 with sides swapped and the #2 at his point (the far leg, the mark and the call-out load over it).
5. **The pin, at every merge.** `house-pin` (v0.0.19's stage 0) is re-recorded at each merge that moves it. Each role's handoff lists its moved cells (sheet, seed, bot, the last tick, the run sheet's hash, the save digest) with the §1 item that moved each, by §0 item 30. A moved cell not on its role's list stops the merge until it is explained. The lead prints every merge's cells in `.run/v020/lead.md`.
6. **The base tree and the patch**, as v0.0.19's:

   ```
   GIT_INDEX_FILE=.run/v020/idx git add -A; git write-tree > .run/v020/base.tree
   ```

   with `.run/v020/stage0.patch`, said in `.run/v020/lead.md`.

## 4. Interfaces

### 4.1 A

```js
// move.js
PIN_GIVE_MS 600, PIN_END_MS 2000
pinOf(state, pid) → { heldMs, by } | null           // the body holding the player's move beat now
// bundle.js
STEP_ASIDE_M 0.6, TWO_PIN_MS 1500, ENTRY_WAIT_MS 400, HEELS_FROM_M 0.2, HEELS_M 0.65, HALL_LEAD_M 0.3, HALL_PAIR_M 2.0
TWO_BLOCK_REPEAT_MS 4000, TWO_OUT_LINE_MS 3000
// route.js
routed(state, pts, { area = routeAreaOf(state), open = [], bodies = [] } = {})   // the built signature (route.js:70) plus one option; bodies: [{ x, z, rM }], discs on C0; pts [from, …, to]
keptOf(state, pid, a, area, keep, dir, v, stopM, st, ms)   // move.js:467, exported as it stands
// carry.js
MASK_R_M 0.3; lineMasked(from, to, bodies, { rM = MASK_R_M } = {}) → body | null
MASK_RESUME_MS 150, MASK_HOLD_MAX_MS 2000, MASK_STEP_M 0.5, MASK_FAULT_MS 300, LIMIT_WARN_MS 500
```

**State** (absent by default): `H.two.masked = { since, by }`; on the leg `L.pins`, `L.masked: [{ atMs, by, ms }]`, `L.twoHeldMs`, `L.heelsMs`. The fault id 'masked'.

### 4.2 B

```js
// groups.js: SITUATIONS.door.five = [['DRILL',1],['DRILL',2],['DRILL',3],['DRILL',4],['DRILL',5]]
// plan.js
planFor(state, pid, gunId, 'cmd:load' | 'cmd:ready' | 'cmd:standby' | 'cmd:stop' | 'cmd:clear', opts)   // SEQ_HOUSE's ids
COLD_ENDS                                              // a literal table by those ids (item 6); never read from MACROS at load
// contact.js
tell(state, pid, key, { atMs, bearingRad, face })      // the one write of mind.contact.told
// model.js
setOpening(state, openingId, s, { atMs, how })         // how: 'push' | 'pull' | 'kick', stored on the delta; absent linear
// the 'door' fact (bundle.js door and force kinds): { …as built, how, leafAtMs, stopAtMs }
// range-items.js
jambMarks(marks, { kind = 'm1' })                      // kind from $look.jamb
// doors.js
leafCurve(how, t) → fraction; the delta's `how`; the door fact's `stopAtMs`
// corner.js
farCoverOf(plan) → { x, z } | null; aidHoldMs(rung, setting = 'rung') → ms; CORNER_POINT 'authored'
STATUS_MS 600, MARK_AT_M 0.3, MARK_H_M 1.5, MOVE_ANSWER_MS 300, MOVE_WAIT_MAX_MS 4000, FAR_COVER_DEG 20, TOLD_MS 3000, TOLD_DEG 20
```

**State** (absent by default): `mind.contact.told = { [key]: { atMs, bearingRad, face } }`; `L.marked = { by, atMs }`; `L.calls = { [wordId]: { due, said } }` (the exit's and the far leg's calls, due when the beat runs, said when its 'say' is emitted, for the TEAM row's "CALLS n OF m"); the opening delta's `how`; `houseLook().marks` (derived, not stored).

### 4.3 C

```js
parOf(state, T) → { ms, base, parts: [{ why: 'head' | 'far', ms }] }

// main.js (v0.0.18's): hitModelOf(s, key, k, 'truth'), passed to houseplan.js by openHouseEnd
houseVerdict(state) → { go, why: [string] }
traceTick(state, R, H, now); debriefOf(state) → { walls, doors, stands, tracks, events, legs, from }

HOUSE_RUNS_MAX 200, RUN_INPUTS_MAX 24000, CALL_BALLOON_MS 1200, MARK_FADE_MS 120
```

## 10. Risks (each owned)

- **The pin moves at every merge** (lead): five sources of movement in one round (§0 item 30). The attributed list per role (§3 step 5) is the safeguard; an unexplained cell stops the merge.
- **The formant voice may sound robotic** (D): voices made by code are hard. The samples V-a to V-d come first, the ship rule keeps V-a the default if the voice fails its gauges, `&voice=old` compares, and the DI's own line stays text.
- **The route round can walk a man into a swing or a wall** (A): `route.js` is the walls' own router and F1, F3 and F26 run over A's holds in `house-flawless-bodies`; a route into a moving leaf's arc is refused and the hand-back taken instead.
- **On his heels, the body gap may hold him more** (A): the #2 at 0.65 m behind you meets the gap guard more often; F45, F46 and F48 run together, and a new hold is a failed gauge, not a tuning.
- **The exit's calls and the far leg add time below rung 3** (B): about +3.5 s a keys lane before item 8's -1.5 s (drill.md §3). F15 and F21 have room (§8); question 8 asks whether the top rungs skip "Moving!".
- **Two new waits** (B's status and far wait, D's PA wait) are dead ends in the making: each has its maximum (`STATUS_MS`, `MOVE_WAIT_MAX_MS` with its hand-back, the PA's line length), and `shoothouse-nodead` runs them in the fuzz.
- **Key 5's meaning changes for the user's fingers** (B): Enter was 27 of the honest bot's 54 door presses in v0.0.17. It moves to T and the fan, where F24 has T's row in one press on 257 of 257 stops. Question 1 asks; one table flips it back.
- **The pars' fit** (C): `ROOM_PAR_K` is the one number fitted against F56. Fitted once, printed, and frozen; a par that a later item moves is reported, never re-fitted in the round.
- **The plan view's size** (C): the round's one L on the UI side; it is last in C's order and under the ship rule.
- **The plaques' slide may hide what the user reads** (C): the TORSO 95% plaque moves off the room, never out of view; its reserved rect is the fall-back, and `ui-house-clear` prints every move.
- **Quick suite time** (every role): about 20 new quick files on a suite near 60 s; the 3 s rule per file, whole lanes heavy.
- **The working tree's lines** (every role): main carries v0.0.18's merges and v0.0.19 moves the #2's code; every hunk is named by function.

1. **The door's five.** P3-j as you drew it on every lane: Breach on 5 (struck "not issued" when you carry none), Enter on T and Tab › 2 › 7? Or Enter on 5 as v0.0.17 built it, or v0.0.19's 5 changing with the loadout? *Default: P3-j as drawn, on every lane.*

3. **The shot.** Of A1 to A4, which bangs as you meant? *Default: A3 in the shoot house (more body in the first 50 ms, the protection's ceiling at -5 dB, no higher at the peak); every other scene keeps v0.0.17's until you score it, since you scored "Bang" on it.*

14. **The lane timer** as a one-line strip while the lane runs, its card at Stop? *Default: yes.*
15. **Your corner.** The aid by rung, always, or off (the Esc menu)? And at room 2, should #1's point be the drawn one or the rule's own, 1.90 m deeper? *Default: by rung; the drawn point, so nothing you have played moves; one switch for the rule's.*
